name: Novelty

subjectOf.text: Suggestions that artificial intelligence will solve the rigidity of centralized reputation systems are misguided and will fail for the same reason, because neural networks are merely a complex mathematical architecture for statistical regression, which is always extremely unreliable when applied to novel situations.
subjectOf.abstract: Suggestions that AI will solve these problems are misguided, and will fail for the same reason. Neural networks are merely a complex mathematical ar- chitecture for performing statistical regression, which is always extremely unreliable when applied to novel situations.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201
scope_conditions: where new social situations continually arise that lie outside the training distribution
subjectOf.status_reason: The claim holds that neural networks are 'always extremely unreliable when applied to novel situations.' Frontier model performance on held-out and adversarially novel tasks between 2023 and 2026 contradicts the unqualified form of this claim. The underlying institutional argument may survive; the empirical premise as stated does not.

subjectOf.text: Middlemen persist rather than being automated away because there are certain junctures in business where novel problems regularly arise whenever circumstances change, requiring creative solutions that people step in to supply, and these persistent junctures become business institutions.
subjectOf.abstract: There are certain junctures in business where novel problems regularly arise when- ever circumstances change. These problems require creative solutions, and people step in to capitalize. These persistent junctures become business institutions.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201

subjectOf.text: No validator, filter, or score in the design is asked about rarity, novelty, frequency, diversity, or coverage, and the outcome is computed by an evaluator alone from a sealed reference that no filter reads.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The oracle alone receives one bit per candidate from the sealed reference, the candidate's true validity verdict.
Validators do see a tag, whose association with rare membership is bounded by design.
